operations.why: it changes what the public sees, to something older, by a person's choice. It is rare, it is never routine, and a second look costs one click. It is also the remedy for a bad forward promotion, so it must stay available: a reviewer delays it, it does not remove it. REVISED 2026-10-02: the owner withdrew P1 — the reviewer is not worth recreating a token and configuring a new Environment. Rollback stays where it is, in v2-promotion, unreviewed.

measured: not an operation. A tombstone is a relation between two releases that promote() and rollback() both record on the pointer they write (atomic_publish.py, def tombstones). Nothing deletes: ConditionalStore has no delete, and retention.py produces plans that no code path executes. The briefing's hypothesis listed it as a third manual operation; there is nothing to gate.

what_this_design_does_not_protect: The v2-promotion key writes AND deletes anywhere in araripe-v2-staging: R2 scope is per bucket, with no prefix, and DELETE comes with WRITE (measured 2026-09-07). The only limit is the code — ConditionalStore has no delete and no unconditional put. Any job on main that names v2-promotion holds that power with no reviewer, which is exactly what the scheduled promotion needs.

Putting the same key pair in a reviewed v2-rollback does not narrow it: the reviewer gates who may START a rollback run, not what the key can do. A change to code on main could call rollback() from a v2-promotion job. What stands between that and the pointer is review of the pull request, not the Environment.

After the cutover the v2-staging key (deposit lane, candidate replay, GEE probe) also writes and deletes in what is then the canonical public bucket, with no reviewer. The pointer is protected from it only by code.

An agent acts as the owner's GitHub account (scopes repo, workflow). GitHub cannot tell the agent's dispatch from the owner's, the main ruleset requires 0 approvals, and a required reviewer can technically be satisfied by the same account. That an agent never merges an unreviewed workflow change and never approves its own Environment run is enforced by AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md, not by GitHub. prevent_self_review must stay false on any Environment whose only reviewer is the owner, or the owner could not approve their own dispatches.

A forward promotion that passes every gate but is scientifically wrong is published without a click. The gates (schema, ledger, checksums, completeness, coverage) are the protection; the remedy is a reviewed rollback, after the fact.
On the site side, deploy authority is push authority on the site main, which has no ruleset; and a private repository on the free plan offers no Environment reviewer at all.

site_side_contradiction.statement: decision D4 (config/phase6_owner_decisions_v1.json) puts the site deploy credential behind a required reviewer. If the routine site deploy ran through that Environment, every routine publication would wait for a click — the same contradiction as condition (2) of the bucket decision, on the other repository.
site_side_contradiction.why_a_deploy_is_needed_per_promotion: the alert index is composed at build time and is not a release object (SITE_ARTIFACT_CONTRACT_V1.md §1); the page compares built-from.json with the live pointer and falls back when they differ
site_side_contradiction.the_window: the cadence has backend detection Mon/Thu 06:00 UTC and the site refresh Tue/Fri 06:00 UTC. If the scheduled promotion follows the deposit and the site rebuild follows the site cron, the page refuses the green index for about 24 h after each promotion — arithmetic on the schedules, not measured, and only if both keep their current days

options.a_workers_builds_on_push: the routine site deploy stays what it is today for the blue path: a push to the site main triggers Cloudflare Workers Builds, whose credential lives in Cloudflare and needs no GitHub Environment; the build composes the index from the route. Not measured: whether the production trigger's build image has the Python that site_artifact.py needs, and whether a build can reach the route. Authority = push to the site main.
options.b_reviewed_ci_deploy: deploy from GitHub Actions through v2-green-deploy with a reviewer. Unavailable on a private free-plan repository, and a click per publication contradicts ROADMAP.md:97. Rejected.
options.c_index_served_at_runtime: the Worker serves the index from R2 instead of from the build. Removes the per-promotion deploy entirely, but it reverses SITE_ARTIFACT_CONTRACT_V1.md §1 ('not a release object'). A contract change: not designed here.

site_side_contradiction.recommendation: a, with the trigger order fixed so the site build follows the promotion rather than a clock; and the pre-cutover fallback-to-blue on a mismatch must be replaced before the blue path is disabled (PACKAGE_P6_PROMPT §4.4 step 3), or after the cutover a mismatch falls back to a source that no longer exists

proposed_decisions.question: replace condition (2) of the 2026-09-30 bucket decision ('required reviewer on v2-promotion') with: promotion stays unreviewed in v2-promotion; rollback moves to a new Environment v2-rollback with the owner as required reviewer, branch policy main, holding the promotion key pair
proposed_decisions.why: condition (2) as written would put a click on every scheduled publication, because v2-promotion serves the whole promotion lane (both jobs that name it are listed in operations[]). The only pointer move that can go backwards is rollback, and only it is never routine.
proposed_decisions.explained_before_deciding: the owner asked when a rollback would be needed and what really needs a click; answered in chat on 2026-10-02: a release that passes every gate but is wrong, expected rare; a rollback does not fix the cause, so it comes with pausing automatic publication; routine needs no click
